name: Imipenem + cilastatin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Imipenem and cilastatin are each about 70% recovered in urine. The US label reduces the dose once creatinine clearance (CrCl) falls below 90 mL/min, raises the seizure warning at CrCl below 30, and says not to give it at CrCl below 15 unless hemodialysis starts within 48 hours. On hemodialysis, use the CrCl 15–29 doses after each session, only when benefit outweighs seizure risk.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses CrCl (mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault); bands at 90, 60, 30 and 15.
chip: Reduce below CrCl 90; avoid <15 off HD

bands.recommendation: CrCl 90 or more: 500 mg every 6 hours or 1 g every 8 hours (susceptible), 1 g every 6 hours (intermediate). CrCl 60–89: 400 mg every 6 hours or 500 mg every 6 hours (susceptible); 750 mg every 8 hours (intermediate) (label Table 3).
CrCl 30–59: 300 mg every 6 hours or 500 mg every 8 hours (susceptible); 500 mg every 6 hours (intermediate) (label Table 3).
CrCl 15–29: 200 mg every 6 hours or 500 mg every 12 hours (susceptible); 500 mg every 12 hours (intermediate). Seizure risk may be higher (label Table 3).
CrCl below 15: do not give unless hemodialysis is started within 48 hours (label).

hd.text: Use the CrCl 15–29 doses (200 mg every 6 hours or 500 mg every 12 hours; 500 mg every 12 hours for intermediate organisms). Give after hemodialysis and time later doses from the end of the session. Recommended only when benefit outweighs seizure risk; monitor closely, especially with CNS disease (label).

pd.text: Information is inadequate to recommend use in peritoneal dialysis (label). For PD-associated peritonitis (ISPD 2022): intraperitoneal intermittent 500 mg in alternate exchanges; continuous loading dose 250 mg/L, then 50 mg/L in each exchange. Specialist input.

crrt.text: Not in label. Li 2020 (Table 3): CVVH ultrafiltration 52 ± 14 mL/kg/h, 1 g every 6 hours; CVVH, CVVHD or CVVHDF at 20 or 37 mL/kg/h, 500 mg every 6 hours for MIC 2 mg/L or less and 1 g every 6 hours for MIC 4–16 mg/L.

dialyzable: Yes: imipenem and cilastatin are both cleared by hemodialysis (label). Protein binding: imipenem about 20%, cilastatin about 40%.
monitoring: CrCl for dose; seizures, myoclonus and confusion, especially at CrCl 30 or less, on dialysis, or with CNS disease (label); valproate levels if coadministered.

pediatric.approved_ages: Neonates and children (non-CNS infections); not recommended for CNS infections (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Up to 3 months (1,500 g or more): under 1 week 25 mg/kg every 12 hours; 1–4 weeks 25 mg/kg every 8 hours; 4 weeks to 3 months 25 mg/kg every 6 hours (label). 3 months and older: 15 to 25 mg/kg every 6 hours (label).

renal.recommendation: Not recommended in children under 30 kg with kidney impairment (no data). 30 kg or more: no pediatric dosing given; specialist input (label).
